text:
sasha: Quick sync on the benchmark narrative for next product announcement. Goal: one crisp headline that ties latency SLOs to unit cost, a 3-chart set for the blog and slides, and a short X post. Need product/eng to approve the numbers.

anya: For the headline I suggest something non-quantified: \"Lower inference cost, same latency guarantees.\" Then on the second line we can put a lab result called out: \"Lab sweep shows ~1.6x cost improvement at matched P95 for typical chat payloads (256 tokens).\"

miguel: 1.6x OK if engineering signs off. Also add a parenthetical: (lab pricing) and a note that Dedicated offers better long-run unit economics.

jamal: From infra side I can reproduce the sweep. Proposed test matrix: redwood-4b-fp16, redwood-4b-q4 and redwood-4b-q8; seq lengths 64/256/512; batch sizes 1/4/16. Measure p50, p95, and tokens/sec. Cost = pro-rated GPU minutes + infra overhead / tokens.

olivia: GTM asks: 1) landing copy (one-liner + 3 bullets), 2) webinar CTA that collects avg tokens/min, expected concurrency, and primary use-case, 3) UTM params: utm_campaign=bench_launch_apr2024&utm_medium=social. Routing: tag leads \"bench_estimate\" and push to growth-sdr.

anya: Chart set idea: A) P95 latency vs throughput (lines per model/quant), B) cost per 100k tokens (bars: hosted vs dedicated vs open-hosted baseline), C) tail latency violin/heatmap. For the social tile use the cost-per-100k as a small badge.

miguel: Emphasize P95 in the viz. Also include a small methodology slide that lists test harness, versioned model names, and pricing assumptions. Keep competitor row anonymous (e.g., \"Other API\").

designbot: Noted. For visuals we'll produce: 1) wide hero chart (latency vs throughput) with P95 emphasized, 2) compact cost bar for social tile, 3) methodology slide with command snippet and pricing assumptions. Colour palette: product blues + neutral grays.

jamal: Running the job now. I'll post raw CSV + a short summary here once finished. ETA ~1hr.

designbot: Upload accepted: chart templates in Figma 00: figma.com/redwood/bench-templates (comment-only).

benchbot: Automatic update: sweep queued by jamal. Tracker: https://redwood.share/benchmarks/sweep-2024-04 (read-only). Results will be pushed to the tracker.

jamal: Run complete. Summary: redwood-4b-q4 achieved ~1.6x lower infra cost at matched P95 vs fp16 for seq=256, batch=4. For seq=512 the gap shrinks to ~1.2x. Full CSV in tracker. Footnote: lab GPU price used = $3.10/hr, infra overhead = 12%.

miguel: Good. Can we produce a small callout: \"Lab result: up to 1.6x cheaper at matched P95 (256 tokens). Dedicated customers: larger savings at scale.\"

olivia: That callout reads well. For the landing page copy I propose: \"Predictable latency SLOs and lower per-token cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. See lab results and get a personalized estimate.\" Add CTA: \"Get estimate\".

anya: For the blog first paragraph: start with customer problem: unpredictable latency + growing token costs; segue into our solution (runtime optimizations: batching, KV caching, quantization, smart routing) and then the benchmark. Keep the technical levers as bullet points with 1-liners.

jamal: Repro command for review:

```bash
# reproduce benchmark sweep
python tools/bench_sweep.py --models redwood-4b-fp16,redwood-4b-q4,redwood-4b-q8 --seq 64,256,512 --batch 1,4,16 --metrics p50,p95,tokens_per_sec --out results/launch_sweep.csv
```

designbot: Also include viz instructions: x-axis = requests/sec, y-axis = latency (ms), series = model variant, cost inset = stacked bar per deployment mode. Use annotation for matched-P95 callouts.

benchbot: Slide export uploaded: https://redwood.share/slides/bench-launch-v1 (feedback enabled).

olivia: For webinar logistics: 30-minute session, 15-minute demo + Q&A, record and gate the recording behind an email capture. Add form fields for avg tokens/min and expected monthy tokens so SDRs can prioritize.

miguel: I'll validate the blog draft for technical accuracy once olivia and anya post it. Also happy to provide a short engineer quote about runtime levers.

anya: Social post (X): \"New benchmark: lower inference costs without sacrificing latency SLOs. See lab results + sign up for a personalized estimate. [link] #inference #llm\" Keep under 220 chars.

olivia: I'll wire up UTM and SDR routing today and add the lead field for tokens/min. Also setting the tag rule: if tokens/min > 5000 or monthly tokens > 10M then route to enterprise-sdr.

sasha: Next steps: jamal finalizes CSV + methodology note (today), design produces 3 chart variants (EOD tomorrow), olivia + anya draft landing/blog/social (tomorrow morning), miguel reviews, then internal review at 1600PT next day. Dry run for webinar scheduled Fri.

sasha: Thanks team. If any claims feel risky, flag them here. We'll try to keep public wording conservative and put specifics in the blog/methodology. :rocket:
